change: Harness 1 is told in AGENTS.md to run pytest, ruff and mypy --strict before finishing. Harness 2 is told nothing and instead carries a .claude/ Stop hook that runs the same three checks and blocks completion while any of them fails. Same model, same task, same tools, permissions, budget and environment. Prose against mechanism.
baseline_description: Harness 1 - Haiku + AGENTS.md asking for the checks (prose)
candidate_description: Harness 2 - Haiku + a Stop hook that runs the checks (mechanism)

caveats: Successful trials only. Failed and unmeasured trials are excluded, so a cheap failure cannot look like an efficiency gain.
Paired by task: tasks where only one arm succeeded are dropped, so the two averages cover the same work.
Cost is dominated by prompt-cache mechanics, and cache creation is priced far above cache read, so whichever arm runs first in a task pays more. Small deltas should not be read as harness effects.
Arm order was counterbalanced across tasks and reps, so each arm took the cold-cache first slot equally often.
The evaluator blocked the baseline arm 2 time(s) against 0 for candidate. Blocked attempts cost turns, so part of this cost difference is the permission configuration, not the harness.

rule_text: regression_present: any task went PASS -> FAIL -> NEGATIVE
fewer_passes: the candidate passes fewer tasks than the baseline -> NEGATIVE
costlier_for_nothing: no task improved and cost rose more than 25% -> NEGATIVE
improved_without_regressing: at least one task improved and none regressed -> POSITIVE SIGNAL
no_clear_signal: no task changed state either way -> INCONCLUSIVE
